summary: Modular monolith: Django + Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL serving None, hosted on Google Cloud Run (us-central1 Iowa). Estimated $50-250/month (within the $400 budget).

architecture_rationale.text: One deployable with strict internal modules for the api_platform domain: a 3-engineer team gets clear boundaries without distributed-system overhead; modules can be extracted later if scale demands it. Over-engineering guard: microservices rejected: 3 engineer(s), no DevOps cannot absorb the operational overhead.

frontend.justification: project.platforms=['api_only']: there is no end-user UI to build; API consumers integrate via the published OpenAPI contract

alternatives.why_not: optional; OpenAPI docs can be generated from the API itself

tradeoffs: Add a server tier later only if dynamic features (forms, auth, comments) appear

backend.justification: Chosen because team already works in python (team.languages); strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=3.

alternatives.why_not: Minimal framework leaves domain structure to the team. Django scores higher on time-to-market and maintainability (fit 6.4 vs 7.5).
A api_platform domain needs a structured service, not scattered functions. Django scores higher on maintainability and security (fit 5.9 vs 7.5).

database.choice: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL (us-central1 Iowa, HA standby)
database.justification: Chosen because relational integrity and transactions for a api_platform domain; strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; strong cost efficiency (4/5) with priorities.cost=3. Managed as Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL: same platform and private network as the application hosting; fully managed: no operations work for a team without DevOps.
